title: Act on Safe Fishing Operations and the Promotion of Safety and Health of Fishing Vessel Crew Members, Etc.
title_original: 어선안전조업 및 어선원의 안전ㆍ보건 증진 등에 관한 법률
full_text:
Act on Safe Fishing Operations and the Promotion of Safety and Health of Fishing Vessel Crew Members, Etc.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to establish a sound fisheries order, maintain and promote the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members, and protect the lives, physical safety, and property of the people by prescribing matters necessary for safe fishing operations and navigation of fishing vessels, the promotion of the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members, and the prevention of accidents. <Amended 2024.1.2>

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act are defined as follows: <Amended 2024.1.2>
1. The term "fishing vessel" means a vessel falling under any item of subparagraph 1 of Article 2 of the Fishing Vessels Act;
1-2. The term "fishing vessel crew member" means a person employed to provide labor on a fishing vessel;
1-3. The term "crew occupational accident" means the death, injury, or illness of a fishing vessel crew member resulting from fishing work or other duties;
1-4. The term "serious crew occupational accident" means a crew occupational accident prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries that is severe, such as one involving death, or that involves a large number of affected fishing vessel crew members;
1-5. The term "fishing vessel owner" means a person who actually operates a fishing business using a fishing vessel;
2. The term "fishing operations" means the capture or collection of aquatic animals or plants at sea using fishing vessels or fishing gear, and the installation of fishing gear or other facilities for such purposes;
3. The term "fishing limit line" means a line prescribed by Presidential Decree that constitutes the northern limit in the East Sea and West Sea up to which fishing operations may be conducted;
4. The term "designated waters" means waters within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree, south of the fishing limit lines in the East Sea and West Sea, in which the fishing operations and navigation of fishing vessels are restricted;
5. The term "fishing restraint line" means a line prescribed by Presidential Decree that constitutes the northern limit of fishing restraint waters in the East Sea and West Sea;
6. The term "fishing restraint waters" means waters within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree, east of the designated waters in the East Sea and west of the designated waters in the West Sea adjacent to the exclusive economic zones (EEZs) of North Korea, Russia, and other countries, in which the fishing operations and navigation of fishing vessels are restricted;
7. The term "general waters" means all waters other than designated waters and fishing restraint waters, excluding overseas waters under subparagraph 10 of Article 2 of the Distant Water Fisheries Development Act;
8. The term "port or harbor" means a port or harbor from or into which a fishing vessel departs or enters (hereinafter referred to as "port departure or entry") for fishing operations, navigation, or other purposes;
9. The term "reporting authority" means a branch station or outpost affiliated with a coast guard station that handles reports of port departure or entry of fishing vessels, or an agency reporting office through which the chief of a coast guard station has a civilian handle port departure or entry reports on the chief's behalf;
10. The term "radio communications enrollment" means the obtaining of a license to establish a radio station under Article 19 of the Radio Waves Act by the owner of a fishing vessel equipped with radio facilities and the enrollment of that owner with the Fishing Vessel Safe Operations Headquarters.

Article 3 (Scope of Application)
This Act shall apply to all fishing vessels owned by nationals of the Republic of Korea (including corporations established under domestic law and foreigners or foreign corporations that have obtained domestic fishing permits or other such authorizations) and by the Government of the Republic of Korea: Provided, That all or part of this Act need not apply to fishing vessels prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as fisheries guidance vessels and fishing vessels engaged in distant water fishing, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2024.1.2>

Article 4 (Relationship to Other Acts)
Except as otherwise expressly provided for in other Acts, safe fishing operations and navigation of fishing vessels shall be governed by this Act: Provided, That this Act shall apply in preference to other Acts with respect to the promotion of the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members and the prevention of accidents. <Amended 2024.1.2>

Article 5 (Duties of the State and Local Governments)
The State and local governments shall have a duty to faithfully perform the following matters to achieve the purposes of this Act: <Amended 2024.1.2>
1. Formulation and implementation of policies necessary for safe fishing operations and navigation of fishing vessels;
2. Formulation and implementation of policies necessary for preventing crew occupational accidents;
3. Preparation of standards for the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members and the prevention of accidents;
4. Modernization of onboard accommodation and living facilities for fishing vessel crew members and improvement of welfare facilities;
5. Other protection and promotion of the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members.

Article 6 (Duties of Fishing Vessel Owners and Crew Members)
(1) Fishing vessel owners shall cooperate with policies established by the State and local governments for safe fishing operations and the prevention of crew occupational accidents, and shall comply with the standards prescribed under this Act for the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members and the prevention of accidents. <Amended 2024.1.2>
(2) Fishing vessel crew members shall comply with policies established by the State and local governments for fishing vessel safety and measures concerning the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members and the prevention of accidents. <Added 2024.1.2>

Article 7 (Formulation of Master Plans for Fishing Vessel Safety, Etc.)
(1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall, in consultation with the heads of relevant administrative agencies, formulate a master plan for fishing vessel safety, etc. (hereinafter referred to as a "master plan") every five years for safe fishing operations and navigation of fishing vessels and for the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members and the prevention of accidents. <Amended 2024.1.2>
(2) A master plan shall include the following matters: <Amended 2024.1.2>
1. Matters concerning medium- and long-term policies for safe fishing vessel operations;
2. The current status of fishing vessel accidents and crew occupational accidents, analysis of their causes, and reduction targets;
3. Matters concerning improvements to systems for safe fishing vessel operations and for the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members and the prevention of accidents;
4. Matters concerning education, publicity, and other activities to prevent fishing vessel accidents and crew occupational accidents;
5. Matters concerning research and development of policies, technologies, and other means for safe fishing vessel operations and the prevention of crew occupational accidents;
6. Detailed annual implementation plans and investment plans for fishing vessel safety and the prevention of crew occupational accidents;
7. Other matters necessary for safe fishing operations and navigation of fishing vessels and for maintaining and promoting the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members.
(3) Matters necessary for the formulation and amendment of master plans under paragraph (1), and other matters necessary for their implementation, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER II REPORTS OF PORT DEPARTURE OR ENTRY, ETC.

Article 8 (Reports of Port Departure or Entry)
(1) The owner or master of a fishing vessel intending to depart from or enter a port or harbor shall file a report with the reporting authority: Provided, That a fishing vessel designated for use as a management vessel under Article 27 (1) of the Fisheries Act or approved for use under paragraph (3) of that Article shall file a report only when departing on a fishing voyage to any of the following waters:
1. Designated waters;
2. Fishing restraint waters;
3. Waters designated by the chief of the competent coast guard station, after consultation with the heads of relevant agencies, as necessary for maintaining public order or national defense.
(2) Notwithstanding paragraph (1), a fishing vessel departing from or entering a port while equipped with and normally operating a fishing vessel position transmitter prescribed by the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard pursuant to the proviso to Article 5-2 (1) of the Fishing Vessels Act shall be deemed to have filed a port departure or entry report under paragraph (1): Provided, That this shall not apply in any of the following cases:
1. Where a report is being filed for the first time;
2. Where there is a change in the contents of the fishing vessel port departure or entry report, such as the list of persons on board;
3. Where the vessel departs on a fishing voyage to designated waters or fishing restraint waters.
(3) The owner or master of a fishing vessel intending to file a port departure or entry report under paragraph (1) shall submit a fishing vessel port departure or entry report stating matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, including the personal details of the reporting person and the list of persons on board.
(4) The procedures and methods for port departure or entry reports under paragraph (1), and other necessary matters, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 8-2 (Provision of Data)
(1) An authority that has received a port departure or entry report under Article 8 shall, upon a request by a fishing vessel crew safety inspector under Article 44 (1) concerning reported matters relating to a vessel within the inspector's scope of duties, provide relevant data, including the list of persons on board, unless there is a justifiable reason not to do so.
(2) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries and the heads of reporting authorities (excluding agency reporting offices) may request data relating to the passport numbers, alien registration numbers, and other such information of foreign fishing vessel crew members from the heads of relevant agencies to perform duties concerning port departure or entry reports under Article 8. In such cases, the heads of relevant agencies receiving such a request shall comply unless there is a compelling reason not to do so. <Added 2025.12.30>
(3) Matters necessary for the scope and methods of provision of data under paragraphs (1) and (2), and other relevant matters, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. <Amended 2025.12.30>

Article 9 (Restrictions on Port Departure or Entry)
(1) No fishing vessel shall depart from or enter a port or harbor in which no reporting authority has been established: Provided, That this shall not apply in cases of unavoidable circumstances, such as seeking shelter from deteriorating weather or drifting due to engine failure.
(2) Where a fishing vessel enters a port or harbor pursuant to the proviso to paragraph (1), its master shall report to a reporting authority located near the port or harbor entered.

Article 10 (Restrictions on Departure, Etc.)
(1) The head of a reporting authority may restrict the departure and fishing operations of fishing vessels when a weather advisory or warning has taken effect for the sea. <Amended 2022.10.18>
(2) When an advance weather advisory or warning (meaning advance notice that the issuance of a weather advisory or warning is expected) or a weather advisory or warning has been issued or taken effect for the sea, the master of a fishing vessel shall comply with safety measures and requirements for fishing vessels prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. <Amended 2022.10.18>
(3) Matters necessary for the criteria, methods, and procedures for restrictions on departure and fishing operations under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. <Amended 2022.10.18>

CHAPTER III RESTRICTIONS ON FISHING OPERATIONS OR NAVIGATION IN DESIGNATED WATERS, ETC.

Article 11 (Prohibition of Crossing the Fishing Limit Line or Fishing Restraint Line)
No fishing vessel shall conduct fishing operations or navigate beyond the fishing limit line or fishing restraint line: Provided, That this shall not apply in cases prescribed by Presidential Decree, such as fishing vessels from areas near the fishing limit line or fishing restraint line.

Article 12 (Registration for a Fishing Voyage)
(1) The owner or master of a fishing vessel intending to conduct fishing operations in designated waters or fishing restraint waters shall register for a fishing voyage with the reporting authority. In such cases, the period of validity of registration for a fishing voyage shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) The procedures and methods for registration for a fishing voyage under paragraph (1), and other relevant matters, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 13 (Restrictions on Fishing Operations or Navigation in Designated Waters)
(1) Where necessary for safe fishing operations and navigation of fishing vessels, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may, after consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, restrict fishing areas and periods by type of fishery in designated waters, and impose other such restrictions.
(2) A person conducting fishing operations in designated waters (including a fishing vessel owner; hereinafter the same shall apply) shall conduct fishing operations or navigate using a fishing vessel equipped with safety equipment prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. <Amended 2024.1.2>
(3) Fishing areas and periods by type of fishery in designated waters under paragraph (1), and other such matters, shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 14 (Restrictions on Fishing Operations or Navigation in Waters Other than Designated Waters)
(1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may, where necessary for safe fishing operations and navigation by fishing vessels, restrict fishing operations or navigation in waters other than designated waters in consultation with the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies.
(2) Fishing vessels setting out for fishing restraint waters in the East Sea shall navigate through general waters south of designated waters, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(3) The waters and periods in which fishing operations or navigation may be restricted under paragraph (1), and other relevant matters, shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 15 (Fishing Operations by Fishing Vessels in Fleets)
(1) Fishing vessels intending to conduct fishing operations in designated waters or fishing restraint waters shall form fleets for departure from port and fishing operations. However, in unavoidable circumstances, such as a breakdown of fishing vessel equipment or an accident involving casualties, they may withdraw from fishing operations in fleets.
(2) A fishing vessel without radio equipment that intends to conduct fishing operations in general waters more than 12 nautical miles from the baseline within the territorial sea under Article 2 of the Territorial Sea and Contiguous Zone Act shall form a fleet with a fishing vessel equipped with radio equipment and report to the reporting authority.
(3) Matters necessary for the methods of forming fleets of fishing vessels, fishing operations in fleets, withdrawal from fleets, and other matters under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 16 (Temporary Restrictions on Fishing Operations or Navigation)
(1) The Minister of National Defense or the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may, where necessary for national security or the maintenance of order, request the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries or a Mayor/Do Governor to restrict fishing operations or navigation in certain waters for a designated period, in consultation with the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries and Metropolitan City Mayors, Do Governors, and Special Self-Governing Province Governors (hereinafter referred to as "Mayors/Do Governors"). However, the Minister of National Defense or the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may restrict fishing operations or navigation where the Minister or the Commissioner General determines that failure to restrict fishing operations or navigation immediately would seriously affect safe fishing operations or navigation by fishing vessels. In such cases, the Minister of National Defense or the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard shall immediately notify the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, the relevant Mayors/Do Governors, and the relevant agencies.
(2) Upon receiving a request under paragraph (1), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries or a Mayor/Do Governor may temporarily restrict fishing operations or navigation, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(3) Matters necessary for the methods and procedures for temporary restrictions on fishing operations and navigation under paragraph (1), and other relevant matters, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 17 (Control of Border Waters in the West Sea)
(1) The commander of the military unit having jurisdiction over the area may, with the cooperation of the reporting authority, control entry into and departure from fishing grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree among the border waters adjoining the Northern Limit Line in the West Sea.
(2) The heads of the relevant agencies having jurisdiction over the fishing grounds specified in paragraph (1) shall endeavor to provide guidance on safe fishing operations, including preventing illegal fishing operations by fishing vessels and their departure from fishing operation areas.
(3) Matters necessary for the scope and methods of control of entry and departure and guidance on safe fishing operations under paragraphs (1) and (2), and other relevant matters, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 18 (Establishment and Operation of Fishing Operations Protection Headquarters)
(1) The Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may establish and operate Fishing Operations Protection Headquarters at Korea Coast Guard offices to handle the following affairs concerning the protection of fishing operations in designated waters:
1. Patrols and enforcement to protect fishing operations;
2. Ascertaining the status of fishing vessel port entry and departure and registration for a fishing voyage, and monitoring the movements of vessels setting out for fishing;
3. Rescue in marine accidents;
4. Detecting and handling unlawful acts by persons conducting fishing operations and notifying the relevant agencies;
5. Controlling catch transport vessels entering and leaving designated waters.
(2) Matters necessary for the establishment and operation of Fishing Operations Protection Headquarters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Chapter IV Projects, Etc. for Safe Fishing Operations and Navigation by Fishing Vessels

Article 19 (Projects for Safe Fishing Operations and Navigation by Fishing Vessels)
(1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may carry out the following projects for safe fishing operations and navigation by fishing vessels:
1. Locating fishing vessels engaged in fishing operations;
2. Providing information on fishing operations;
3. Providing guidance on safe fishing operations, including preventing fishing vessels from crossing the fishing limit line or fishing restraint line and from being captured;
4. Projects to support integrated maritime defense;
5. Managing fishing vessels operating in Korea-Japan and Korea-China exclusive economic zones (EEZ);
6. Providing safe fishing operations education for fishers;
7. Operating radio equipment systems to prevent fishing vessel accidents and facilitate prompt rescue;
8. Operating and managing the comprehensive fishing vessel safety management system;
9. Other projects deemed necessary by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
(2) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may entrust some of the projects under paragraph (1) to the National Federation of Fisheries Cooperatives established under the Fisheries Cooperatives Act (hereinafter referred to as the "National Federation"). In such cases, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may provide the National Federation with support for the necessary expenses.
(3) The National Federation may establish and operate Fishing Vessel Safe Operations Headquarters (hereinafter referred to as the "Safety Headquarters") to perform the affairs entrusted under paragraph (2).

Article 20 (Guidance and Supervision)
(1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may provide guidance and supervision regarding the affairs under the jurisdiction of the Safety Headquarters.
(2) Where deemed necessary, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may require reports on matters concerning the affairs, accounts, and property of the Safety Headquarters, or have public officials under the Minister's authority inspect the books, documents, or other articles of the Safety Headquarters.

Article 21 (Radio Communications Enrollment and Position Notification by Fishing Vessels)
(1) The owner of a fishing vessel equipped with radio equipment under Article 5 of the Fishing Vessels Act shall complete radio communications enrollment with the Safety Headquarters having jurisdiction over the port or harbor primarily used by the fishing vessel for entry and departure, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(2) When a fishing vessel enrolled in radio communications under paragraph (1) departs from port, it shall notify the Safety Headquarters of its position at the designated times.
(3) Where a fishing vessel fails to fulfill its obligation to notify its position by the time designated under paragraph (2), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall take necessary measures, such as ascertaining the position of the fishing vessel and notifying search and rescue agencies and other relevant bodies.
(4) The frequency and procedures for position notification for each sea area under paragraph (2), the methods of ascertaining positions under paragraph (3), and the methods and procedures for notification to search and rescue agencies and other relevant bodies shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 22 (Duties of Masters)
(1) The master of a fishing vessel (hereinafter referred to as the "master") shall listen to emergency warnings by the methods prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(2) Where a master receives information about a dangerous situation or notification to evacuate from any of the following vessels or the Safety Headquarters, the master shall immediately comply, and a fishing vessel equipped with radio equipment shall notify the Safety Headquarters of its evacuation status without delay:
1. Fisheries guidance vessels of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries or local governments;
2. Vessels of Korea Coast Guard offices;
3. Naval vessels.

Article 23 (Stopping Vessels, Etc.)
(1) Where a fishing vessel is deemed to have violated this Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, the Minister of National Defense, and the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may issue necessary orders or take necessary measures, such as stopping the vessel or conducting an onboard investigation.
(2) Matters necessary for the methods of signaling an order to stop a vessel and for onboard investigations under paragraph (1), and other relevant matters, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 24 (Wearing Life Jackets, Etc.)
(1) A person on board a fishing vessel shall, when on a deck exposed to the outside, wear a life jacket or lifesaving garment for safe fishing operations and navigation. <Amended 2022.10.18, 2025.12.30>
(2) In the case of paragraph (1), the master of a fishing vessel shall ensure that persons on board the fishing vessel wear a life jacket or lifesaving garment. <Newly inserted 2022.10.18>
(3) In the case of paragraph (1), the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may have persons prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries check whether persons on board a fishing vessel are wearing a life jacket or lifesaving garment. <Amended 2022.10.18>

Article 25 (Safe Fishing Operations Education)
(1) The owner of a fishing vessel and its master, chief engineer, chief radio officer, or a person performing such duties on their behalf shall complete the education necessary to maintain order in fishing operations and ensure safe fishing operations (hereinafter referred to as "safe fishing operations education").
(2) The types of safe fishing operations education under paragraph (1), the institutions providing such education, the methods of conducting it, and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Chapter IV-2 Management System for the Safety and Health of Fishing Vessel Crew Members and Accident Prevention <Newly inserted 2024.1.2>

Article 26 (Standards for the Safety and Health of Fishing Vessel Crew Members and Accident Prevention)
(1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall formulate standards for the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members and accident prevention (hereinafter referred to as "Crew Safety and Health Standards") that include the following matters:
1. Work and hygiene standards to ensure the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members;
2. Standards for safety and health measures by fishing vessel owners;
3. Risk assessment standards for identifying hazards to fishing vessel safety;
4. Other matters necessary for the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members and accident prevention.
(2) When formulating or amending the Crew Safety and Health Standards, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall consult with representatives of fishing vessel owner organizations and fishing vessel crew member organizations.
(3) The details of the Crew Safety and Health Standards shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 27 (Fishing Vessel Supervisors) A fishing vessel owner shall require a person in a position responsible for duties relating to the fishing operations and navigation of the fishing vessel and who directly manages and supervises fishing vessel crew members (hereinafter referred to as a "fishing vessel supervisor") to perform the duties prescribed by Presidential Decree concerning the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members.

Article 28 (Conducting Risk Assessments)
(1) A fishing vessel owner shall identify harmful and hazardous factors arising from the fishing vessel's hull and its appurtenances, machinery, instruments, and equipment (hereinafter referred to as "hull, etc."), the work activities of fishing vessel crew members, and other duties, and assess whether the magnitude of the risk that could lead to injury or disease is within an acceptable range.
(2) A fishing vessel owner shall take measures pursuant to this Act and orders issued under this Act according to the results of the assessment under paragraph (1), and shall take additional measures where necessary to prevent danger or impairment of health to fishing vessel crew members.
(3) When conducting the assessment under paragraph (1), a fishing vessel owner shall have the fishing vessel crew members of the workplace concerned participate, as determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
(4) A fishing vessel owner shall record and retain the results of the assessment under paragraph (1) and the measures taken under paragraph (2), as determined by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
(5) The methods, procedures, and timing of the assessment under paragraph (1), and other necessary matters, shall be determined and publicly notified by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 29 (Installation and Affixing of Fishing Vessel Safety and Health Signs)
(1) A fishing vessel owner shall install or affix signs displaying, through pictures, symbols, letters, or similar means, warnings concerning harmful or dangerous places, facilities, or substances aboard a fishing vessel, instructions or guidance for responding to emergencies, or other matters to raise fishing vessel crew members' awareness of safety and health (hereinafter referred to as "fishing vessel safety and health signs"), in a manner that fishing vessel crew members can readily recognize. In such cases, a fishing vessel owner who employs foreign fishing vessel crew members who do not hold the nationality of the Republic of Korea shall prepare fishing vessel safety and health signs in the native languages of those foreign fishing vessel crew members, as determined by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
(2) The types, shapes, colors, uses, and locations for installing and affixing fishing vessel safety and health signs, and other necessary matters, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 30 (Establishment and Operation of an Integrated Information System for the Prevention of Crew Occupational Accidents, Etc.)
(1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may establish and operate an integrated information system for the prevention of crew occupational accidents in order to prevent crew occupational accidents in a systematic and efficient manner.
(2) Matters concerning the establishment and operation of the integrated information system under paragraph (1), and other necessary matters, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 31 (Safety Measures)
(1) A fishing vessel owner shall take the necessary measures (hereinafter referred to as "safety measures") to prevent crew occupational accidents arising from any of the following risks:
1. The risk of accidents involving falls overboard due to entanglement in fishing gear lines, loss of footing, or similar causes;
2. The risk of accidents involving bodily collisions with fishing gear, ropes, structures, or similar objects;
3. The risk of accidents involving the body being caught in net haulers;
4. The risk of accidents during diving work, such as asphyxiation;
5. Other risks of accidents arising from work performed on fishing vessels.
(2) Necessary matters concerning the safety measures that a fishing vessel owner shall take under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 32 (Health Measures)
(1) A fishing vessel owner shall take the necessary measures (hereinafter referred to as "health measures") to prevent any of the following health impairments:
1. Health impairment caused by raw materials, gases, dust, oxygen deficiency, pathogens, or similar factors;
2. Health impairment caused by high temperatures, low temperatures, noise, vibration, abnormal atmospheric pressure, or similar factors;
3. Health impairment caused by simple repetitive work or work that places an excessive burden on the human body;
4. Health impairment caused by a failure to maintain appropriate standards for ventilation, natural lighting, illumination, thermal insulation, moisture protection, cleanliness, or similar matters.
(2) Necessary matters concerning the health measures that a fishing vessel owner shall take under paragraph (1) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 33 (Compliance by Fishing Vessel Crew Members with Safety Measures and Health Measures)
Fishing vessel crew members shall comply with the measures prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries among the measures taken by the fishing vessel owner under Articles 31 and 32.

Article 34 (Orders to Formulate and Implement Fishing Vessel Safety and Health Improvement Plans)
(1) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries deems it necessary to take comprehensive improvement measures to prevent crew occupational accidents with respect to a fishing vessel falling under any of the following, the Minister may order the fishing vessel owner to formulate and implement a plan to improve the safety of the fishing vessel and the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members (hereinafter referred to as a "fishing vessel safety and health improvement plan"), as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries:
1. A fishing vessel whose crew occupational accident rate is higher than the average accident rate for vessels in the same tonnage class in the same business category;
2. A fishing vessel on which a serious crew occupational accident has occurred because the fishing vessel owner failed to implement necessary safety measures or health measures;
3. A fishing vessel on which the number of persons who have developed occupational diseases is at least the number prescribed by Presidential Decree.
(2) When formulating a fishing vessel safety and health improvement plan, a fishing vessel owner shall have the plan deliberated on by the Fishing Vessel Safety and Health Committee under Article 36. However, for a fishing vessel on which no Fishing Vessel Safety and Health Committee has been established, the fishing vessel owner shall hear the opinions of a representative of fishing vessel crew members elected with the affirmative votes of a majority of the fishing vessel crew members aboard.

Article 35 (Submission of Written Fishing Vessel Safety and Health Improvement Plans, Etc.)
(1) A fishing vessel owner who has been ordered to formulate and implement a fishing vessel safety and health improvement plan under Article 34(1) shall prepare a written fishing vessel safety and health improvement plan and submit it to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(2) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall examine a written fishing vessel safety and health improvement plan submitted under paragraph (1), as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, and notify the fishing vessel owner of the results in writing. In such cases, where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries deems it necessary to maintain and promote the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members, the Minister may order supplementation of the written fishing vessel safety and health improvement plan concerned.
(3) Fishing vessel owners and fishing vessel crew members shall comply with the written fishing vessel safety and health improvement plan examined under the first sentence of paragraph (2) (including a written fishing vessel safety and health improvement plan supplemented under the second sentence of that paragraph).

Article 36 (Fishing Vessel Safety and Health Committee)
(1) A fishing vessel owner shall establish and operate a Fishing Vessel Safety and Health Committee to deliberate and decide on important matters concerning the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members.
(2) Fishing vessel owners and fishing vessel crew members shall faithfully implement matters deliberated and decided on by the Fishing Vessel Safety and Health Committee.
(3) A Fishing Vessel Safety and Health Committee shall not deliberate or decide on matters in a manner contrary to this Act, orders issued under this Act, collective agreements, or rules of employment.
(4) A fishing vessel owner shall not subject a member of the Fishing Vessel Safety and Health Committee to disadvantageous treatment for reasons related to the performance of the member's duties.
(5) The fishing vessels required to establish a Fishing Vessel Safety and Health Committee, the matters subject to its deliberation and decision, and necessary matters concerning its composition and operation shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 37 (Emergency Measures by Fishing Vessel Owners, Etc.)
(1) Where there is an imminent risk of a crew occupational accident, a fishing vessel owner or fishing vessel supervisor shall take the measures necessary for safety and accident prevention, such as immediately stopping the work of fishing vessel crew members and evacuating fishing vessel crew members from the fishing vessel.
(2) Where a fishing vessel crew member suffers an injury or develops an illness while serving aboard a vessel, the fishing vessel owner or fishing vessel supervisor shall take measures for medical care, including immediate and appropriate treatment.
(3) Necessary matters concerning the methods and procedures for the measures under paragraphs (1) and (2) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 38 (Stoppage of Work by Fishing Vessel Crew Members)
(1) Where there is an imminent risk of an accident, a fishing vessel crew member may stop work and evacuate.
(2) A fishing vessel crew member who has stopped work and evacuated under paragraph (1) shall report that fact to the fishing vessel supervisor without delay.
(3) Upon receiving a report under paragraph (2), the fishing vessel supervisor shall take the necessary measures concerning the safety of fishing vessel crew members.
(4) A fishing vessel owner shall not dismiss or otherwise subject to disadvantageous treatment a fishing vessel crew member who has stopped work and evacuated under paragraph (1), where the crew member has reasonable grounds to believe that there is an imminent risk of an accident.

Article 39 (Corrective Measures by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, Etc.)
(1) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries determines that a fishing vessel owner's failure to take the necessary measures prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries concerning the safety of the fishing vessel's hull, etc. is likely to cause significant harm or danger to fishing vessel crew members, the Minister may order suspension of use, replacement, or removal of the hull, etc. concerned, improvements to facilities, or other necessary measures concerning safety and health prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries (hereinafter referred to as "corrective measures").
(2) A fishing vessel owner who has been ordered to take corrective measures under paragraph (1) shall post the particulars of the order for corrective measures in a place aboard the fishing vessel that fishing vessel crew members can easily see, until the corrective measures concerning the hull, etc. concerned are completed.
(3) Where a fishing vessel owner's failure to comply with an order for corrective measures concerning the hull, etc. concerned results in a harmful or dangerous condition not being eliminated or improved, or creates a risk that harm or danger to fishing vessel crew members will significantly increase, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may order the suspension of all or part of the work related to the hull, etc. concerned.
(4) A fishing vessel owner who has been ordered to suspend use under paragraph (1) or suspend work under paragraph (3) may, upon completing the corrective measures, request that the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries lift the suspension of use under paragraph (1) or the suspension of work under paragraph (3).
(5) Where the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries determines, in response to a request for lifting a suspension under paragraph (4), that the corrective measures have been completed, the Minister shall lift the suspension of use under paragraph (1) or the suspension of work under paragraph (3).

Article 40 (Measures by Fishing Vessel Owners in the Event of a Serious Crew Occupational Accident)
(1) In the event of a serious crew occupational accident, a fishing vessel owner shall take the necessary measures concerning safety and health, such as immediately stopping the work concerned and evacuating fishing vessel crew members from the place of work.
(2) Where a fishing vessel owner becomes aware that a serious crew occupational accident has occurred, the owner shall report it to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries without delay, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries. However, if an unavoidable circumstance, such as a natural disaster, arises, the owner shall report it without delay once that circumstance ceases to exist.

Article 41 (Suspension of Fishing Operations or Navigation by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries in the Event of a Serious Crew Occupational Accident)
(1) In the event of a serious crew occupational accident, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may order the suspension of fishing operations or navigation if the Minister determines that there is an imminent risk of another crew occupational accident because the fishing vessel owner has failed to take the measures under Article 37(1).
(2) In unavoidable circumstances, such as where a serious crew occupational accident has occurred due to a fire, explosion, or similar cause and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries determines that the crew occupational accident may spread to the area surrounding the fishing vessel on which it occurred, the Minister may order the suspension of fishing operations or navigation of the fishing vessel concerned and the evacuation of fishing vessel crew members.
(3) Where a fishing vessel owner requests that a suspension of fishing operations or navigation under paragraph (1) or (2) be lifted, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall lift the suspension of fishing operations or navigation under paragraph (1) or (2), as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(4) Necessary matters concerning the procedures and methods for requesting the lifting of a suspension of fishing operations or navigation under paragraph (3) shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 42 (Investigation into the Causes of Serious Crew Occupational Accidents, Etc.)
(1) In the event of a serious crew occupational accident, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may investigate the causes of its occurrence in order to ascertain those causes or establish measures to prevent crew occupational accidents.
(2) No person shall damage the scene of a serious crew occupational accident or obstruct the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries' investigation into its causes under paragraph (1).
(3) The content and procedures of an investigation into the causes of a serious crew occupational accident with respect to the fishing vessel on which it occurred, and other necessary matters, shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 43 (Prohibition of Concealment of the Occurrence of Crew Occupational Accidents; Reporting, Etc.)
(1) Where a crew occupational accident has occurred, a fishing vessel owner shall not conceal the fact of its occurrence.
(2) A fishing vessel owner shall record and retain the causes of crew occupational accidents and other relevant matters, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.
(3) With respect to crew occupational accidents prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, a fishing vessel owner shall report an outline of the occurrence, its causes, plans for preventing recurrence, and other relevant matters to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries.

Article 44 (Fishing Vessel Crew Safety Inspectors)
(1) The Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries shall have fishing vessel crew safety inspectors for the supervision of the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members.
(2) Necessary matters concerning the qualifications, appointment and removal, duties, and other aspects of fishing vessel crew safety inspectors shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 45 (Powers of Fishing Vessel Crew Safety Inspectors)
(1) A fishing vessel crew safety inspector may require a fishing vessel owner, a fishing vessel crew member, or any other relevant person to appear, or order the submission of books or documents, and may enter a fishing vessel or any other place of business to conduct inspections or ask questions, for the purpose of supervising the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members under this Act.
(2) When entering and conducting an inspection pursuant to paragraph (1), the fishing vessel crew safety inspector shall notify the person subject to the inspection of the inspection plan, including the date, time, purpose, and details of the inspection, at least seven days before commencing the inspection: Provided, That such notification may be dispensed with in an emergency or where it is deemed that advance notification of the inspection could prevent the purpose of the inspection from being achieved due to the destruction of evidence or other reasons.
(3) A fishing vessel crew safety inspector entering and conducting an inspection pursuant to paragraph (1) shall carry identification indicating his or her authority and present it to the relevant persons, and shall, upon entry, show the relevant persons a document stating his or her name, the time of entry, the purpose of entry, and other relevant particulars.

Article 46 (Duty of Confidentiality, Etc.)
(1) A person who is or was a fishing vessel crew safety inspector shall not disclose any confidential information learned in the course of performing his or her duties.
(2) A fishing vessel crew safety inspector shall perform his or her duties fairly and independently.
(3) A fishing vessel crew safety inspector shall not perform duties in which he or she has a direct or indirect interest in connection with the supervision of the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members.

Article 47 (Reporting to Supervisory Authorities)
(1) Where this Act or any order issued under this Act has been violated on a fishing vessel, a fishing vessel crew member may report the violation to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries or a fishing vessel crew safety inspector.
(2) A fishing vessel owner shall not dismiss a fishing vessel crew member or subject him or her to any other adverse treatment on the grounds that the crew member has made a report under paragraph (1).

CHAPTER V SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS <Added on Jan. 2, 2024>

Article 48 (Financial Support)
(1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries or the head of a local government may provide subsidies or loans within budgetary limits where deemed necessary to prevent accidents involving fishing vessels and casualties.
(2) Projects eligible for support under paragraph (1) and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 49 (Administrative Dispositions)
(1) Where a person who has obtained a permit or license to engage in fishing under the Fisheries Act or in aquaculture under the Aquaculture Industry Development Act, has filed a report of fishing, or has registered a catch transportation business falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may request the head of the local government having jurisdiction over matters concerning the relevant fishing or aquaculture permit, license, report, or registration (hereinafter referred to as a "fishing permit, etc.") to cancel the fishing permit, etc. or suspend it for a specified period not exceeding three months: <Amended on Oct. 18, 2022>
1. Where the person fails to make a port departure or entry report under Article 8 (1) and (2) or makes a false report;
2. Where the person violates the restrictions on port departure and fishing operations under Article 10 (1) or fails to comply with the safety measures and requirements to be observed for fishing vessels under paragraph (2) of that Article;
3. Where the person violates the prohibition against crossing the fishing limit line or fishing restraint line under Article 11;
4. Where the person departs on a fishing voyage without registration for a fishing voyage under Article 12 or obtains such registration by false or other improper means;
5. Where the person violates the restrictions on fishing operations or navigation in designated waters under Article 13;
6. Where the person violates the restrictions on fishing operations or navigation in waters other than designated waters under Article 14;
7. Where the person fails to form a fleet to conduct fishing operations or leaves a fleet without justifiable grounds, in violation of Article 15;
8. Where the person violates the temporary restrictions on fishing operations or navigation under Article 16;
9. Where the person fails to comply with controls over border waters in the West Sea under Article 17;
10. Where the person violates an order to stop a vessel or fails to comply with necessary measures, including an onboard inspection, under Article 23.
(2) The head of a local government who receives a request to cancel or suspend a fishing permit, etc. under paragraph (1) shall comply with the request unless there are justifiable grounds for not doing so.

Article 50 (Guidance and Enforcement Concerning Violations)
(1) The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may provide guidance and take enforcement action against persons conducting fishing operations in violation of any order, disposition, restriction, or condition under this Act. In such cases, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may have fisheries supervisory officials under Article 69 of the Fisheries Act perform such guidance and enforcement duties. <Amended on Jan. 11, 2022>
(2) Except as otherwise provided in this Act, the relevant provisions of the Fisheries Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to fisheries supervisory officials.

Article 51 (Delegation of Authority)
The Minister of Oceans and Fisheries or the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard may delegate part of his or her authority under this Act to the heads of affiliated agencies or the heads of local governments, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

CHAPTER VI PENALTY PROVISIONS <Added on Jan. 2, 2024>

Article 52 (Penalties)
(1) Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than seven years or by a fine not exceeding 100 million won:
1. A person who causes the death of a fishing vessel crew member in violation of Article 31 (1);
2. A person who causes the death of a fishing vessel crew member in violation of Article 32 (1).
(2) A person who commits an offense under paragraph (1) again within five years after a sentence imposed for an offense under that paragraph becomes final and conclusive shall be punished by increasing the penalty prescribed for that offense by up to one half.

Article 53 (Penalties)
Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than five years or by a fine not exceeding 50 million won:
1. A person who fails to take safety measures in violation of Article 31 (1);
2. A person who fails to take health measures in violation of Article 32 (1);
3. A person who fails to take necessary measures, including suspension of work or provision of medical care, in violation of Article 37 (1) or (2);
4. A person who fails to comply with an order to suspend work relating to the hull, etc. under Article 39 (3);
5. A person who fails to take necessary measures upon the occurrence of a serious crew occupational accident, in violation of Article 40 (1);
6. A person who fails to comply with an order of the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries under Article 41 (1) or (2);
7. A person who dismisses a fishing vessel crew member or subjects him or her to any other adverse treatment, in violation of Article 47 (2).

Article 54 (Penalties)
A person who fails to comply with an order to take corrective measures under Article 39 (1) shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than three years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won.

Article 55 (Penalties)
Any of the following persons shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than one year or by a fine not exceeding 10 million won: <Amended on Jan. 2, 2024>
1. A person who conducts fishing operations or navigates beyond the fishing limit line or fishing restraint line, in violation of Article 11;
2. A person who conducts fishing operations or navigates in designated waters, in violation of Article 13;
3. A person who fails to comply with controls over border waters in the West Sea, in violation of Article 17;
4. A person who violates an order to stop a vessel or fails to comply with necessary measures, including an onboard inspection, in violation of Article 23;
5. A person who damages the scene of a serious crew occupational accident or obstructs the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries in investigating its causes, in violation of Article 42 (2);
6. A person who conceals the occurrence of a crew occupational accident, or instigates or conspires to conceal its occurrence, in violation of Article 43 (1).

Article 56 (Penalties)
A person who discloses confidential information learned in the course of performing his or her duties, in violation of Article 46 (1), shall be punished by a fine not exceeding 10 million won.

Article 57 (Joint Penalty Provisions)
Where the representative of a corporation, or an agent, employee, or other worker of a corporation or individual commits a violation falling under Article 52 (1) or any of Articles 53 through 55 in connection with the business of the corporation or individual, in addition to punishing the violator, the corporation shall be punished by a fine as specified in the following subparagraphs, and the individual shall be punished by the fine prescribed in the relevant Article: Provided, That this shall not apply where the corporation or individual has not neglected to exercise due care and supervision over the relevant business to prevent the violation. <Amended on Jan. 2, 2024>
1. In the case of Article 52 (1): A fine not exceeding one billion won;
2. In the case of Articles 53 through 55: The fine prescribed in the relevant Article.

Article 58 (Administrative Fines)
(1) A person who fails to report the occurrence of a serious crew occupational accident or makes a false report, in violation of Article 40 (2), shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 30 million won. <Added on Jan. 2, 2024>
(2) A person who fails to report the causes of a crew occupational accident or other relevant matters, or makes a false report, in violation of Article 43 (3), shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 15 million won. <Added on Jan. 2, 2024>
(3) A person who fails to comply with an order to formulate and implement a fishing vessel safety and health improvement plan under Article 34 (1) shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding 10 million won. <Added on Jan. 2, 2024>
(4) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding five million won: <Amended on Jan. 2, 2024>
1. A person who fails to complete radio communications enrollment with the Safety Headquarters, in violation of Article 21 (1);
2. A person who fails to notify the Safety Headquarters of the vessel's position or makes a false notification, in violation of Article 21 (2);
3. A person who receives danger and evacuation signals from a fisheries guidance vessel, patrol vessel, or the Safety Headquarters and fails to comply with them, in violation of Article 22 (2);
4. A person who fails to have a fishing vessel supervisor perform duties concerning the safety and health of fishing vessel crew members, in violation of Article 27;
5. A person who fails to install or affix fishing vessel safety and health signs, in violation of Article 29 (1);
6. A person who fails to undergo deliberation by the Fishing Vessel Safety and Health Committee or hear the opinion of the representative of fishing vessel crew members when formulating a fishing vessel safety and health improvement plan, in violation of Article 34 (2);
7. A person who fails to comply with the written fishing vessel safety and health improvement plan, in violation of Article 35 (3);
8. A person who fails to post the matters specified in an order to take corrective measures, in violation of Article 39 (2).
(5) Any of the following persons shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding three million won: <Amended on Jan. 2, 2024>
1. A person who departs from or enters a port or harbor where no reporting authority has been established, in violation of the main clause of Article 9 (1);
2. A person who fails to make a report to a reporting authority near the port or harbor entered, in violation of Article 9 (2);
3. A person who fails to listen to emergency warnings, in violation of Article 22 (1);
4. A person who fails to wear a life jacket or lifesaving garment, in violation of Article 24 (1);
5. A person who fails to ensure that a life jacket or lifesaving garment is worn, in violation of Article 24 (2);
6. A person who fails to complete education on safe fishing operations, in violation of Article 25;
7. A person who fails to comply with measures prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, in violation of Article 33.
(6) A person who fails to comply with a request to appear under Article 45 (1), refuses, obstructs, or evades entry into a fishing vessel or any other place of business, fails to comply with an order to submit books or documents, submits false books or documents, or makes a false statement shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding two million won. <Added on Jan. 2, 2024>
(7) Administrative fines under paragraphs (1) through (6) shall be imposed and collected by the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, the Commissioner General of the Korea Coast Guard, or the head of a Si/Gun/Gu, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended on Jan. 2, 2024>

ADDENDA <Act No. 16569, Aug. 27, 2019>
